ulna, ulnae f.

noun, first declension

an ell, a length measured on the arm; Traupman’s word for the yard

Literally the forearm (see forearm); as a measure, an ell. Lewis & Short notes that Pliny also uses it for a fathom, as much as a man can clasp with both arms.

See also forearm, yard.

SourcesLewis & Short: ulna

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 409.
